title: substring bounds
explanation: Half-open ranges [start, end) are everywhere in Java: substring, copyOfRange, subList. The length is always `end - start`.

title: Letter index
prompt: Complete the classic count-array idiom for lowercase letters.
explanation: 26 slots for a-z; `c - 'a'` maps 'a'→0 ... 'z'→25. This exact loop opens Valid Anagram and many others.

title: Why StringBuilder
prompt: Building an n-character string with `result += c` in a loop is O(n²). Why?
options: Strings are immutable, so each += copies the entire string built so far
The += operator is slow for all types
The garbage collector runs after every +=
It isn't — the compiler optimizes it to O(n)
explanation: Each concatenation allocates a fresh string and copies 1+2+...+n ≈ n²/2 characters total. StringBuilder appends into a growable buffer: O(n) overall.

title: Count the vowels
prompt: Return how many characters of `s` are vowels (`a e i o u`, lowercase input). Loop with `charAt`, or `toCharArray()` with an enhanced for.

solution.explanation: `"aeiou".indexOf(c) >= 0` is a compact alternative to the chain of ==.

title: Drill: reverse a string
prompt: From memory, two idioms in one: convert to `char[]`, two-pointer swap in place, return `new String(chars)`. (Yes, `new StringBuilder(s).reverse().toString()` also works — know both; write the manual one here.)
hints: `s.toCharArray()` gives you a mutable copy; `new String(chars)` converts back.

title: Drill: letter frequency array
prompt: From memory: return the count of the most frequent character in `s` (lowercase letters only, non-empty). Build the `int[26]` count array, then scan it for the max.

solution.explanation: Count array + scan: the two-pass shape you'll reuse in Valid Anagram, Longest Repeating Character Replacement, and more.

hints: First loop fills `counts[c - 'a']++`, second loop finds the max.

title: Recall: string access
prompt: Fill in the length, character, and substring operations.
code:
int n = s.{{1}}();          // string length (WITH parentheses)
char c = s.{{2}}(0);        // first character
String pre = s.{{3}}(0, 3); // first 3 chars, [0, 3)
explanation: Strings use `length()` (a method, unlike arrays); `charAt(i)` reads one char; `substring(start, end)` takes the half-open range.

title: Drill: last character
prompt: From memory: return the last character of `s` (non-empty) as a String. Use `charAt` and `length()`.
hints: `String.valueOf(char)` turns a char into a String.

title: Recall: search & split
prompt: Fill in the search and split operations.
code:
int i = s.{{1}}("b");         // first index of "b", or -1
boolean has = s.{{2}}("ab");  // is "ab" a substring?
String[] parts = s.{{3}}(" "); // break on spaces
explanation: `indexOf` returns the first position (or -1), `contains` gives a boolean, `split` breaks the string into a `String[]`.

title: Drill: count words
prompt: From memory: return the number of space-separated words in `s` (0 if empty). Use `split(" ")`.
hints: Guard the empty string (split would give `[""]`, length 1).

title: Recall: StringBuilder
code:
StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
sb.{{1}}("ab");                 // add text
sb.{{2}}(sb.length() - 1);      // remove the last char
String out = sb.{{3}}();        // final String
explanation: `append` adds, `deleteCharAt(length-1)` pops the last char (key for backtracking), `toString` produces the final String.

title: Drill: build with StringBuilder
prompt: From memory: return the string `"ab"` repeated `n` times, built with a StringBuilder in a loop (never `+=` in a loop!).
hints: Create the builder before the loop, `append` inside, `toString` after.
